CLOUD REVIEWER seat for PR #2463 of tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, at head 67b8659dac9a550ab3edae856568b56f8cfcbd58. Bus nonce: c275b5643b5e7be8d0edfbd4202d16ee. Never send push notifications.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fix-review.md and its rules from main, and follow them exactly. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin 67b8659dac9a550ab3edae856568b56f8cfcbd58`; the PR body is in the PR. Verify each claim adversarially: mutate the fix and check the tests fail, and check every figure in the body at this head. Check that it merges with origin/main (`git merge-tree --write-tree`) and read CI on this head from the check-runs API.
Output: in a fresh directory of your own (`W=$(mktemp -d)`), write verdict.md, whose first line is exactly `Fix review: merge 67b8659dac9a550ab3edae856568b56f8cfcbd58` or `Fix review: blocked 67b8659dac9a550ab3edae856568b56f8cfcbd58 <class>: <reason>` (no brackets; the class is lower-case letters and dashes), in the format the role file gives, then a blank line, then `bus-nonce: c275b5643b5e7be8d0edfbd4202d16ee`; put the evidence in `ev/` beside it. Do NOT run bus.sh: its dispatch record lives on the orchestrator's machine, which publishes the verdict there (cloud_relay.sh). Return the verdict on a probe ref, and push nothing else; this builds one parentless commit with a private index and touches no branch of your checkout: `R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); G=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir); mkdir -p $W/pr && cp -r $W/verdict.md $W/ev $W/pr/ && cd $W/pr && T=$(GIT_DIR=$G GIT_INDEX_FILE=$W/idx GIT_WORK_TREE=$W/pr sh -c 'git add -A -f . && git write-tree') && C=$(GIT_DIR=$G git -c user.name=seat -c user.email=seat@users.noreply.github.com commit-tree $T -m "verdict 2463 67b8659dac9a550ab3edae856568b56f8cfcbd58") && git -C $R push -q origin $C:refs/heads/probe/rev-2463-c275b564`. That ref is the return signal. Do not post comments, approve or merge.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
Production fix for the v7.0.1 regression where the monthly savings entity reads extremely negative. Root cause: #2411's MonthlyLedger._coverage_factor returns max(1.0, month_hours/settled), which explodes on a store upgraded mid-month (few hour samples). Fix: fall back to pro_rata when hour samples are fewer than spot samples (custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/ledger.py:328). Check that the predicate is sound for every store history: fresh install, mid-month upgrade, full month, a month with gaps, and DST months. Check that it cannot under- or over-state savings in the normal case, and that pro_rata is the right fallback (not a silent mask). Mutate the predicate (BOOLOP, CMP_BOUND, GUARD_OFF) and check that the tests/features.py checks fail. Also check the flat-price null control, and that mutation-autofix will pin the three unpinned sites named in the body. The owner's diagnostics export is private: never ask for it or build fixtures from it.
